claim: Sensory maps in layer (L) 2/3 of rodent cortex lack precise functional column boundaries.
source: Sensory maps in layer (L) 2/3 of rodent cortex lack precise functional column boundaries, and instead exhibit locally heterogeneous (salt-and-pepper) tuning superimposed on smooth global topography.
evidence: This is a statement in the abstract that is supported by citations to prior work in the introduction and by the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Sensory maps in L2/3 of rodent cortex exhibit locally heterogeneous (salt-and-pepper) tuning superimposed on smooth global topography.
source: Sensory maps in layer (L) 2/3 of rodent cortex lack precise functional column boundaries, and instead exhibit locally heterogeneous (salt-and-pepper) tuning superimposed on smooth global topography.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in the manuscript showing dispersed tuning in L2/3 and by citations to prior studies.

claim: Normally housed mice had a dispersed, salt-and-pepper whisker map in L2/3.
source: Normally housed mice had a dispersed, salt-and-pepper whisker map in L2/3, but L4 was more topographically precise.
evidence: This is directly supported by imaging data presented in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: L4 was more topographically precise than L2/3 in normally housed mice.
source: Normally housed mice had a dispersed, salt-and-pepper whisker map in L2/3, but L4 was more topographically precise.
evidence: This is supported by imaging data comparing L2/3 and L4 shown in Figures 2 and 3.

claim: Enrichment from P21 to P46-71 sharpened whisker tuning in L2/3.
source: Enrichment (P21 to P46-71) sharpened whisker tuning and decreased, but did not abolish, local tuning heterogeneity.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figures 3 and 4 showing sharper receptive fields in enriched mice.

claim: Enrichment decreased, but did not abolish, local tuning heterogeneity in L2/3.
source: Enrichment (P21 to P46-71) sharpened whisker tuning and decreased, but did not abolish, local tuning heterogeneity.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 3 showing reduced but still present salt-and-pepper organization after enrichment.

claim: Enrichment strengthened and sharpened whisker point representations in L2/3.
source: In L2/3, enrichment strengthened and sharpened whisker point representations, and created functional boundaries of tuning similarity and noise correlations at column edges.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2 showing enhanced responses in the home column and reduced responses at flanks.

claim: Enrichment created functional boundaries of tuning similarity at column edges in L2/3.
source: In L2/3, enrichment strengthened and sharpened whisker point representations, and created functional boundaries of tuning similarity and noise correlations at column edges.
evidence: This is supported by signal correlation data in Figure 5 showing sharper transitions at column boundaries.

claim: Enrichment created functional boundaries of noise correlations at column edges in L2/3.
source: In L2/3, enrichment strengthened and sharpened whisker point representations, and created functional boundaries of tuning similarity and noise correlations at column edges.
evidence: This is supported by noise correlation data in Figure 5 showing reduced correlations across columns after enrichment.

claim: Enrichment drives emergence of functional columnar topography in S1.
source: Thus, enrichment drives emergence of functional columnar topography in S1, and reduces local tuning heterogeneity.
evidence: This is the main conclusion supported by data in Figures 2-5 showing enhanced columnar organization after enrichment.

claim: Enrichment reduces local tuning heterogeneity in S1.
source: Thus, enrichment drives emergence of functional columnar topography in S1, and reduces local tuning heterogeneity.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 3 showing increased fraction of cells tuned to the columnar whisker.

claim: Changes from enrichment predict better touch detection by neural populations within each column.
source: These changes predict better touch detection by neural populations within each column.
evidence: This is supported by neural decoder analysis in Figure 7 showing improved detection performance in enriched mice.

claim: Sensory maps may enable efficient local network computations.
source: Sensory maps are a defining feature of cortical sensory areas, and may enable efficient local network computations (Chklovskii and Koulakov, 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior theoretical work.

claim: Maps for sensory features in L2/3 of primary sensory cortex in rodents exhibit strong tuning heterogeneity between nearby neurons.
source: In rodents, maps for sensory features in L2/3 of primary sensory cortex exhibit strong tuning heterogeneity between nearby neurons, superimposed on a smoothly varying global topography.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies and by the experimental data in this manuscript.

claim: In rodent L2/3 sensory maps, discrete functional column boundaries are lacking.
source: In these maps, discrete functional column boundaries are lacking and the neural ensemble activated by a single sensory feature is spatially dispersed.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data in Figures 2-3 and citations to prior work.

claim: The neural ensemble activated by a single sensory feature is spatially dispersed in rodent L2/3.
source: In these maps, discrete functional column boundaries are lacking and the neural ensemble activated by a single sensory feature is spatially dispersed.
evidence: This is supported by experimental data showing salt-and-pepper organization in Figures 2-3.

claim: Appropriate sensory experience is often required for development of topography.
source: Appropriate sensory experience is often required for development of topography (Katz and Shatz, 1996), and L2/3 maps are robustly plastic to sensory experience (Buonomano and Merzenich, 1998; Feldman and Brecht, 2005; LeMessurier and Feldman, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies on experience-dependent development.

claim: L2/3 maps are robustly plastic to sensory experience.
source: Appropriate sensory experience is often required for development of topography (Katz and Shatz, 1996), and L2/3 maps are robustly plastic to sensory experience (Buonomano and Merzenich, 1998; Feldman and Brecht, 2005; LeMessurier and Feldman, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies demonstrating L2/3 plasticity.

claim: Whiskers are tactile sensors represented in S1 by a topographic array of cortical columns.
source: Whiskers are tactile sensors represented in S1 by a topographic array of cortical columns, each centered on a L4 barrel.
evidence: This is established knowledge about the whisker-barrel system in rodents.

claim: Each whisker column in S1 is centered on a L4 barrel.
source: Whiskers are tactile sensors represented in S1 by a topographic array of cortical columns, each centered on a L4 barrel.
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge about the barrel cortex.

claim: In the canonical whisker map, nearly all neurons are tuned for their column's anatomically-corresponding whisker.
source: In the canonical whisker map, inferred from single-unit recordings, nearly all neurons are tuned for their column's anatomically-corresponding whisker.
evidence: This is based on prior single-unit recording studies, as indicated by the context.

claim: Recent cellular-resolution population calcium imaging studies in L2/3 reveal that while average tuning within each column is topographically correct, tuning of individual neurons within each column is heterogeneous.
source: However, recent studies using cellular-resolution population calcium imaging in L2/3 reveal that while average tuning within each column is topographically correct, tuning of individual neurons within each column is heterogeneous, with intermixed neurons tuned for either the columnar whisker or local surround whiskers.
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent imaging studies.

claim: The set of neurons tuned for one whisker is dispersed across multiple columns in L2/3 without discrete functional column borders.
source: The set of neurons tuned for one whisker is dispersed across multiple columns in L2/3 without discrete functional column borders (Sato et al., 2007; Clancy et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior imaging studies.

claim: The dispersed whisker representation in L2/3 resembles salt-and-pepper maps of orientation tuning and retinotopy in rodent V1.
source: This globally smooth but locally scattered representation resembles salt-and-pepper maps of orientation tuning and retinotopy in rodent V1 (Ohki et al., 2005; Bonin et al., 2011) and frequency tuning in rodent A1 (Kanold et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citations to studies in V1 and A1.

claim: Environmental enrichment and exercise increase the amount, complexity and salience of sensory stimuli.
source: In particular, environmental enrichment and exercise increase the amount, complexity and salience of sensory stimuli, and promote cortical development (Diamond et al., 1976).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work on enrichment effects.

claim: Environmental enrichment promotes cortical development.
source: In particular, environmental enrichment and exercise increase the amount, complexity and salience of sensory stimuli, and promote cortical development (Diamond et al., 1976).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work.

claim: Enrichment sharpens single-unit receptive fields in forepaw S1 and A1 of young rodents.
source: Enrichment sharpens single-unit receptive fields and refines average map topography in forepaw S1 and A1 of young rodents (Coq and Xerri, 1998; Engineer et al., 2004; Cai et al., 2009; Jakkamsetti et al., 2012), and in whisker S1 of adults (Polley et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Enrichment refines average map topography in forepaw S1 and A1 of young rodents.
source: Enrichment sharpens single-unit receptive fields and refines average map topography in forepaw S1 and A1 of young rodents (Coq and Xerri, 1998; Engineer et al., 2004; Cai et al., 2009; Jakkamsetti et al., 2012), and in whisker S1 of adults (Polley et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Enrichment sharpens receptive fields in whisker S1 of adult rodents.
source: Enrichment sharpens single-unit receptive fields and refines average map topography in forepaw S1 and A1 of young rodents (Coq and Xerri, 1998; Engineer et al., 2004; Cai et al., 2009; Jakkamsetti et al., 2012), and in whisker S1 of adults (Polley et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Polley et al., 2004.

claim: GCaMP6s was expressed in L2/3 pyramidal cells using Drd3-Cre mice.
source: We expressed GCaMP6s in either L2/3 pyramidal (PYR) cells or L4 excitatory cells of S1 by injecting Cre-dependent GCaMP6s virus into either Drd3-Cre mice for L2/3 PYR cell-specific expression or Scnn1a-Tg3-Cre mice for L4 excitatory-specific expression (Gong et al., 2007; Madisen et al., 2010; Adesnik et al., 2012).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used in the study.

claim: GCaMP6s was expressed in L4 excitatory cells using Scnn1a-Tg3-Cre mice.
source: We expressed GCaMP6s in either L2/3 pyramidal (PYR) cells or L4 excitatory cells of S1 by injecting Cre-dependent GCaMP6s virus into either Drd3-Cre mice for L2/3 PYR cell-specific expression or Scnn1a-Tg3-Cre mice for L4 excitatory-specific expression (Gong et al., 2007; Madisen et al., 2010; Adesnik et al., 2012).
evidence: This describes the experimental method used in the study.

claim: Imaging was performed under anesthesia while applying calibrated whisker deflections.
source: Imaging was performed under anesthesia, while applying calibrated whisker deflections.
evidence: This describes the experimental conditions.

claim: Nine whiskers in a 3 × 3 grid centered on D2 were deflected in random order.
source: We randomly interleaved deflection of 9 whiskers in a 3 × 3 grid centered on D2, using brief 5-pulse deflection trains, plus no-stimulation 'blank' trials (50–70 repetitions of each stimulus) (Figure 1A–C).
evidence: This describes the stimulus protocol used in the study.

claim: GCaMP6s-based receptive fields were similar to spiking-based receptive fields in 9 out of 10 whisker-responsive L2/3 neurons tested.
source: We confirmed that GCaMP6s-based receptive fields were similar to spiking-based receptive fields by simultaneous juxtacellular spike recording and GCaMP6s imaging in 10 whisker-responsive L2/3 neurons. Receptive fields from spike counts were highly similar to those from ΔF/F in 9/10 cells (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is supported by simultaneous recording and imaging data shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Enriched mice were housed with 4–5 tactile toys and 2–3 littermates.
source: EN mice were housed with 4–5 tactile toys and 2–3 littermates, while NH mice were housed with a single littermate and no toys (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the enrichment housing conditions.

claim: Normally housed mice were housed with a single littermate and no toys.
source: EN mice were housed with 4–5 tactile toys and 2–3 littermates, while NH mice were housed with a single littermate and no toys (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This describes the normal housing conditions.

claim: Imaging was performed after 25–50 days of enrichment or normal housing experience.
source: Imaging was performed after 25–50 days of EN or NH experience (Figure 1A).
evidence: This describes the experimental timeline.

claim: In L2/3 of normally housed mice, the point representation was centered on the reference whisker's anatomical column and fell off gradually over several columns' distance.
source: For L2/3 cells in normally-housed (NH) mice (11 imaging fields, seven mice, 998 total cells, 475 responsive cells, age: P56 ± 11), the point representation was centered on the reference whisker's anatomical column, and fell off gradually over several columns' distance.
evidence: This is supported by data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Enriched mice showed an elevated mean response in the reference column and just around it compared to normally housed mice in L2/3.
source: Enriched (EN) mice (11 imaging fields, seven mice, 1257 total cells, 874 responsive cells, age: P63 ± 16) showed an elevated mean response in the reference column and just around it.
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 2A showing higher responses in central bins.

claim: Enrichment increased mean responses in L2/3 at 0–75 μm from column center (NH: 0.59 ± 0.06, EN: 0.77 ± 0.04; p=0.0098).
source: This was observed in the central bin (0–75 μm from column center; NH: 0.59 ± 0.06, EN: 0.77 ± 0.04; p=0.0098, permutation test for difference in means) as well as at 150–225 µm (NH: 0.53 ± 0.02, EN: 0.60 ± 0.02; p=0.0028) and 225–300 µm (NH: 0.41 ± 0.02, EN: 0.51 ± 0.01; p=0.0001).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the point representation analysis.

claim: Enrichment suppressed mean responses at the flanks of the point representation in L2/3 (375–750 μm, p<0.05 for all bins).
source: But EN suppressed mean responses at the flanks of the point representation (375–750 μm, p<0.05 for all bins) (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the point representation analysis shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Enrichment sharpened the point representation in L2/3.
source: Thus, enrichment sharpened the point representation in L2/3.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the data in Figure 2A-B showing enhanced central responses and reduced flank responses.

claim: In L4 of normally housed mice, the point representation was sharper than in L2/3.
source: L4 is expected to contain a more spatially precise whisker map than L2/3 (Simons, 1978; Andrew Hires et al., 2015), but this has not been tested with cellular-resolution imaging. We imaged L4 cells in Scnna1-Cre mice. We imaged from 107 responsive cells in L4 of NH mice (six imaging fields, five mice, 322 total cells, age: P70 ± 16). We found that the point representation was sharper in L4 than L2/3 (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is supported by imaging data in Figure 2C and citations to prior studies.

claim: In enriched mice, enrichment reduced mean whisker-evoked responses in L4 for cells in most bins <375 μm from the reference whisker's column center (p<0.05 for each bin).
source: In EN mice, we imaged from 181 responsive cells in L4 (eight imaging fields, six mice, 586 total cells, age: P58 ± 5). We found that EN reduced mean whisker-evoked responses for cells in most bins <375 μm from the reference whisker's column center (p<0.05 for each bin), including at 0–75 μm (NH: 1.11 ± 0.13, EN: 0.86 ± 0.06, p=0.034) (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from L4 imaging data shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Enrichment generally weakened L4 whisker responses, rather than sharpening the point representation relative to its central peak.
source: Thus, enrichment generally weakened L4 whisker responses, rather than sharpening the point representation relative to its central peak.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the L4 data in Figure 2C-D.

claim: Enrichment did not alter mean barrel radius in Drd3-Cre mice (NH: 151 ± 7.2 μm, EN: 145 ± 4.6 μm, p=0.7).
source: Enrichment did not alter mean barrel radius (NH: 151 ± 7.2 μm, n = 6 mice, EN: 145 ± 4.6 μm [mean ± SEM], n = 7 mice (2-way ANOVA, factors: enrichment and barrel identity, p=0.7 for enrichment factor) (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from anatomical measurements shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: Enrichment did not alter barrel radius in Scnn1a-Cre mice (NH: 118 ± 6.6 μm, EN: 124 ± 6.9 μm, p=0.01).
source: There was also no change in barrel radius in Scnn1a-Cre mice, which have a slightly smaller barrels (NH: 118 ± 6.6 μm, n = 5 mice, EN: 124 ± 6.9 μm, n = 6 mice, p=0.01 for enrichment factor).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from anatomical measurements.

claim: The functional changes in L2/3 point representation occurred without gross changes in L4 barrel dimensions.
source: Thus, the functional changes in L2/3 point representation occurred without gross changes in L4 barrel dimensions.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the barrel size measurements in Figure 2—figure supplement 2.

claim: 53% of responsive L2/3 cells within 0–75 µm of a column center in normally housed mice had a best whisker that matched the columnar whisker.
source: 53% (31/58) of responsive cells within 0–75 µm of a column center had a BW that matched the column's anatomically-mapped whisker (termed the columnar whisker, CW).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from tuning analysis in normally housed mice.

claim: 67% of L2/3 PYR cells within 0–75 µm of the column center in normally housed mice were tuned to the columnar whisker using the statistically equivalent best whisker criterion.
source: By this measure, 67% (39/58) of L2/3 PYR cells within 0–75 µm of the column center were tuned to the CW.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from tuning analysis using the eBW criterion.

claim: 63% of L4 excitatory cells in normally housed mice had a best whisker that matched the columnar whisker.
source: 63% of L4 excitatory cells (30/48) had a BW that matched the CW, and 73% (35/48) had the CW among the eBWs.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from L4 tuning analysis.

claim: The fraction of cells tuned to a given whisker fell off approximately 30% more sharply with distance in L4 than in L2/3.
source: However, the fraction of cells tuned to a given whisker fell off ~30% more sharply with distance in L4 than in L2/3, using either tuning measure. This difference was significant at distance bins from 150 to 375 µm from the column center (p<0.05, Fisher's Exact Test) (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is a quantitative comparison between L2/3 and L4 shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: L4 exhibits more topographic precision in whisker tuning of single cells than L2/3.
source: Thus, L4 exhibits more topographic precision in whisker tuning of single cells than L2/3.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the comparison of tuning precision between L2/3 and L4.

claim: In enriched mice, 82% of L2/3 cells located 0–75 μm from a column center were tuned to the columnar whisker, which is greater than in normally housed mice (67%, p=0.025).
source: In EN mice, 82% (111/135) of cells located 0–75 μm from a column center were tuned to the CW, which is greater than NH mice (67%, p=0.025, Fisher's Exact Test).
evidence: This is a quantitative result comparing enriched and normally housed mice shown in Figure 3A.

claim: 77.1% of whisker-responsive cells within column boundaries in enriched mice were tuned to the columnar whisker, compared to 65.1% in normally housed mice (p=0.00008).
source: When all cells located within column boundaries were considered together (irrespective of distance to center), 77.1% (468/607) of whisker-responsive cells in EN mice were tuned to the CW, compared to 65.1% (224/344) in NH (p=0.00008).
evidence: This is a quantitative result showing enrichment increased tuning precision.

claim: Enrichment increased L2/3 map precision, particularly in the home column of each whisker, but did not abolish salt-and-pepper tuning.
source: Thus, EN increased L2/3 map precision, particularly in the home column of each whisker, but did not abolish salt-and-pepper tuning (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the tuning data in Figure 3A.

claim: In enriched mice, 90% of L4 cells at column centers (0–75 μm) were tuned to the columnar whisker, which is greater than the 73% in normally housed mice (p=0.021).
source: In EN mice, 90% (57/63) of cells at column centers (0–75 μm) were tuned to the CW, which is greater than the 73% in NH mice (p=0.021) (Figure 3C–D).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from L4 tuning analysis shown in Figure 3C-D.

claim: In enriched mice, 89.3% of all L4 cells within a column boundary were columnar whisker-tuned, compared to 75.6% in normally housed mice (p=0.0086).
source: In EN mice, 89.3% (133/149) of all cells within a column boundary were CW-tuned, compared to 75.6% (65/86) in NH mice (p=0.0086).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from L4 tuning analysis.

claim: Enrichment increased tuning precision in L4.
source: Thus, despite the expectation that L4 is less plastic than L2/3 (Glazewski and Fox, 1996; Feldman and Brecht, 2005), enrichment also increased tuning precision in L4.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on L4 tuning data, with citations to prior work on L4 plasticity.

claim: In L2/3, enrichment increased responses to the strongest three whiskers and decreased responses to the weakest three whiskers, relative to normally housed cells.
source: In L2/3, EN increased responses to the strongest three whiskers, and decreased responses to the weakest three whiskers, relative to NH cells (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by rank-ordered receptive field data in Figure 4A.

claim: Receptive fields were sharper, on average, in enriched mice compared to normally housed mice in L2/3.
source: Thus, receptive fields were sharper, on average, in EN mice.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the rank-ordered receptive field analysis in Figure 4A.

claim: Enrichment increased the signal-to-noise of both columnar whisker response and the best 2 surround whisker responses in L2/3.
source: EN specifically increased the signal-to-noise of both CW response and the best 2 SW responses (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4B.

claim: Enrichment decreased spontaneous (blank trial) activity relative to normally housed mice in L2/3.
source: In addition to these changes in tuning shape, EN also decreased spontaneous (blank trial) activity relative to NH (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4C.

claim: Columnar whisker responses were higher in enriched than normally housed mice in L2/3 (NH: 0.64 ± 0.03, EN: 0.71 ± 0.02; p=0.01).
source: CW responses were higher in EN than NH (NH: 0.64 ± 0.03, EN: 0.71 ± 0.02; p=0.01, permutation test for difference in means).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from receptive field analysis in L2/3.

claim: Enrichment reduced responses to the surround whisker one row dorsal to the columnar whisker in L2/3 (within-arc, −1 row: NH: 0.44 ± 0.02, EN 0.35 ± 0.02, p=0.001).
source: EN reduced responses to both these SWs (within-arc, −1 row: NH: 0.44 ± 0.02, EN 0.35 ± 0.02, p=0.001; within-arc, +one row: NH: 0.39 ± 0.02, EN: 0.29 ± 0.01, p=0.0001).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from receptive field analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Enrichment increased responses to the surround whisker one arc rostral of the columnar whisker in L2/3 (within-row, +one arc: NH: 0.34 ± 0.01, EN: 0.53 ± 0.02, p=0.0001).
source: In the within-row dimension, EN increased responses to the SW one arc rostral of the CW (within-row, +one arc: NH: 0.34 ± 0.01, EN: 0.53 ± 0.02, p=0.0001), and did not alter responses to the SW one arc caudal of the CW (within-row, −1 arc: NH: 0.57 ± 0.04, EN 0.55 ± 0.04, p=0.40).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from receptive field analysis shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Enrichment broadened receptive fields in the within-row dimension in L2/3.
source: Thus, EN broadened receptive fields in the within-row dimension (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the receptive field data in Figure 4D.

claim: In L4, enrichment reduced responses to most whiskers in rank-ordered receptive fields.
source: In L4, EN reduced responses to most whiskers in rank-ordered receptive fields (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4A for L4.

claim: In L4, responses to the best surround whisker were reduced somewhat more than responses to the columnar whisker by enrichment.
source: Responses to the best surround whisker were reduced somewhat more than responses to the CW (Figure 4A–B), and spontaneous activity was unaffected (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 4A-C for L4.

claim: Columnar whisker responses were weaker in enriched than normally housed mice in L4 (NH: 0.98 ± 0.09, EN: 0.81 ± 0.04, p=0.02).
source: When receptive fields were examined in somatotopic space, CW responses were weaker in EN than NH (NH: 0.98 ± 0.09, EN: 0.81 ± 0.04, p=0.02), as were responses to the within-row, +one arc SW (NH: 0.54 ± 0.08, EN: 0.17 ± 0.02, p=0.0001), the within-row, −1 arc SW (NH: 0.67 ± 0.13, EN 0.33 ± 0.04, p=0.003), and the within-arc, +one row SW (NH: 0.23 ± 0.03, EN 0.11 ± 0.02, p=0.0007).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from L4 receptive field analysis.

claim: Enrichment sharpened L4 receptive fields by a global weakening of whisker responses, unlike in L2/3.
source: Thus, EN sharpened L4 receptive fields, but by a global weakening of whisker responses, unlike in L2/3.
evidence: This is a conclusion comparing enrichment effects in L4 versus L2/3.

claim: The enrichment effect in L4 differs from adult enrichment in rats, which shrinks whisker receptive fields in L2/3 but not L4.
source: This effect differs from adult enrichment in rats, which shrinks whisker receptive fields in L2/3 but not L4 (Polley et al., 2004).
evidence: This is a comparison to prior work cited from Polley et al., 2004.

claim: Prior imaging studies detected a global tuning gradient in L2/3 of S1 but no functional boundaries at anatomical column edges.
source: Prior imaging studies detected a global tuning gradient in L2/3 of S1 but no functional boundaries at anatomical column edges (Kerr et al., 2007; Sato et al., 2007).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior imaging studies.

claim: In normally housed mice, mean signal correlation for L2/3 neuron pairs fell off modestly with intersoma distance.
source: In NH mice, mean signal correlation for neuron pairs fell off modestly with intersoma distance, and was slightly higher for within-column pairs than across-column pairs.
evidence: This is supported by signal correlation data in Figure 5A.

claim: For closely spaced L2/3 pairs (<150 μm apart) in normally housed mice, signal correlation was only modestly higher for within-column pairs than across-column pairs (0.652 ± 0.005 vs. 0.611 ± 0.007, p<0.0001).
source: For closely spaced pairs (<150 μm apart) signal correlation was only modestly higher for within-column pairs than across-column pairs (0.652 ± 0.005 vs. 0.611 ± 0.007, p<0.0001, permutation test of difference in means), reflecting the lack of functional column boundaries (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from signal correlation analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: In enriched mice, mean signal correlation for within-column L2/3 pairs was modestly increased (NH: 0.637 ± 0.004, EN: 0.659 ± 0.002; p<0.0001).
source: In EN mice, mean signal correlation for within-column pairs was modestly increased (NH: 0.637 ± 0.004, EN: 0.659 ± 0.002; includes pairs at all distances; p<0.0001, permutation test), while signal correlation for across-column pairs was greatly reduced (NH: 0.541 ± 0.004, EN: 0.425 ± 0.004; p<0.0001) (Figure 5A,C).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from signal correlation analysis shown in Figure 5A,C.

claim: In enriched mice, signal correlation for across-column L2/3 pairs was greatly reduced (NH: 0.541 ± 0.004, EN: 0.425 ± 0.004; p<0.0001).
source: In EN mice, mean signal correlation for within-column pairs was modestly increased (NH: 0.637 ± 0.004, EN: 0.659 ± 0.002; includes pairs at all distances; p<0.0001, permutation test), while signal correlation for across-column pairs was greatly reduced (NH: 0.541 ± 0.004, EN: 0.425 ± 0.004; p<0.0001) (Figure 5A,C).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from signal correlation analysis shown in Figure 5A,C.

claim: In enriched mice, signal correlation for closely spaced cross-column L2/3 pairs (<150 μm apart) was much lower than for similarly spaced within-column pairs (0.674 ± 0.003 vs. 0.529 ± 0.006, p<0.0001).
source: Moreover, signal correlation for closely spaced cross-column pairs (<150 μm apart) was much lower than for similarly spaced within-column pairs (0.674 ± 0.003 vs. 0.529 ± 0.006, p<0.0001) (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from signal correlation analysis shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Enrichment generated a tuning boundary at column edges in L2/3.
source: Thus, EN generated a tuning boundary at column edges.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the signal correlation data in Figure 5.

claim: Noise correlations measure shared, stimulus-independent trial-to-trial variability between neurons, likely reflecting shared functional input.
source: EN also generated columnar structure in noise correlations, which measure shared, stimulus-independent trial-to-trial variability between neurons, likely reflecting shared functional input (Averbeck et al., 2006; Kohn et al., 2016).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work on noise correlations.

claim: In normally housed mice, noise correlations for L2/3 neuron pairs decreased with distance and were similar within columns (0.334 ± 0.002) and across columns (0.327 ± 0.002).
source: In NH mice, noise correlations for L2/3 neuron pairs decreased with distance, and were similar within columns (0.334 ± 0.002) and across columns (0.327 ± 0.002).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from noise correlation analysis.

claim: Enrichment modestly reduced noise correlations for within-column L2/3 pairs (to 0.307 ± 0.001; p<0.0001 vs. NH).
source: EN modestly reduced noise correlations for within-column pairs (to 0.307 ± 0.001; p<0.0001, permutation test vs. NH), but greatly reduced noise correlations for cross-column pairs (to 0.255 ± 0.001; p<0.0001, permutation test vs. NH).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from noise correlation analysis shown in Figure 5B,D.

claim: Enrichment greatly reduced noise correlations for cross-column L2/3 pairs (to 0.255 ± 0.001; p<0.0001 vs. NH).
source: EN modestly reduced noise correlations for within-column pairs (to 0.307 ± 0.001; p<0.0001, permutation test vs. NH), but greatly reduced noise correlations for cross-column pairs (to 0.255 ± 0.001; p<0.0001, permutation test vs. NH).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from noise correlation analysis shown in Figure 5B,D.

claim: Enrichment substantially reduced signal and noise correlations for L2/3 neurons outside the reference column to neurons inside the column.
source: In NH, neurons outside the reference column exhibited fairly high signal and noise correlations to the neurons inside the column. EN substantially reduced these signal and noise correlations for neurons outside the column, while preserving signal correlation and only modestly reducing noise correlation among neurons within the reference column (Figure 5E–F).
evidence: This is supported by spatial maps of correlations in Figure 5E-F.

claim: Enrichment generated a stronger gradient of signal- and noise-correlation in L2/3 at the reference column edge.
source: This generated a stronger gradient of signal- and noise-correlation in L2/3 at the reference column edge (Figure 5G–H).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 5G-H showing steeper correlation gradients.

claim: In L4, enrichment generally increased correlations between co-columnar neurons.
source: In L4 of Scnn1a-Cre mice, EN generally increased correlations between co-columnar neurons (Figure 6).
evidence: This is supported by data in Figure 6.

claim: Enrichment increased signal correlations between co-columnar neurons in L4 (NH: 0.681 ± 0.011; EN: 0.774 ± 0.005; p<0.0001).
source: This was true for both signal correlations (NH: 0.681 ± 0.011; EN: 0.774 ± 0.005; p<0.0001) and noise correlations (NH: 0.241 ± 0.006; EN: 0.356 ± 0.002; p<0.0001).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from L4 correlation analysis shown in Figure 6.

claim: Enrichment increased noise correlations between co-columnar neurons in L4 (NH: 0.241 ± 0.006; EN: 0.356 ± 0.002; p<0.0001).
source: This was true for both signal correlations (NH: 0.681 ± 0.011; EN: 0.774 ± 0.005; p<0.0001) and noise correlations (NH: 0.241 ± 0.006; EN: 0.356 ± 0.002; p<0.0001).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from L4 correlation analysis shown in Figure 6.

claim: Enrichment drove functional differentiation of columns in L2/3.
source: Thus, EN drove functional differentiation of columns in L2/3, and increased coordinated activity within each column in L4.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the correlation data in Figures 5 and 6.

claim: Enrichment increased coordinated activity within each column in L4.
source: Thus, EN drove functional differentiation of columns in L2/3, and increased coordinated activity within each column in L4.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the L4 correlation data in Figure 6.

claim: The major effects of enrichment were robust to different levels of neuropil correction in both L2/3 and L4.
source: To confirm that the major effects of the study were robust to different levels of neuropil correction, we applied neuropil subtraction in both L2/3 and L4 at three weights (r = 0, r = 0.3, r = 0.7, see Materials and methods) (Figure 5—figure supplement 2). Enrichment effects on tuning heterogeneity (Figure 3) and point representation (Figure 5) were qualitatively unchanged across these levels of neuropil subtraction in both L2/3 and L4 (Figure 5—figure supplement 2A–D).
evidence: This is supported by analysis in Figure 5—figure supplement 2 testing robustness to methodological choices.

claim: Enrichment improved detection of columnar whisker deflections by spatially clustered L2/3 pyramidal cell ensembles located in column centers.
source: Enrichment improved detection of CW deflections by spatially clustered PYR ensembles located in column centers (Figure 7).
evidence: This is supported by neural decoder analysis in Figure 7.

claim: Enrichment increased both absolute detection accuracy and coding efficiency such that in enriched mice, smaller ensembles were needed for equivalent detection performance.
source: Enrichment increased both absolute detection accuracy and coding efficiency such that in EN mice, smaller ensembles were needed for equivalent detection performance.
evidence: This is supported by decoder performance data in Figure 7C.

claim: The strengthening of columnar whisker-evoked responses, the reduction of spontaneous activity and noise correlations, and the higher proportion of columnar whisker-tuned neurons are sufficient to improve single-trial coding of whisker deflections in enriched mice.
source: Thus, the strengthening of CW-evoked responses, the reduction of spontaneous activity and noise correlations, and the higher proportion of CW-tuned neurons are sufficient to improve single-trial coding of whisker deflections in EN mice.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the decoder analysis in Figure 7.

claim: Enrichment improved detection by ensembles in the home whisker column, but worsened detection by ensembles in neighboring columns.
source: Topographically, enrichment improved detection by ensembles in the home whisker column, but worsened detection by ensembles in neighboring columns (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is supported by decoder performance as a function of distance in Figure 7D.

claim: The columnar organization of effective decoding was sharpened by enrichment, matching the sharper point representations in L2/3 of enriched S1.
source: Thus, the columnar organization of effective decoding was sharpened, matching the sharper point representations in L2/3 of enriched S1.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the decoder analysis in Figure 7D.

claim: The dispersed, salt-and-pepper, weakly columnar somatotopy in L2/3 of S1 is partially a product of impoverished experience in standard laboratory housing.
source: These results indicate that the dispersed, salt-and-pepper, weakly columnar somatotopy in L2/3 of S1 is partially a product of impoverished experience in standard laboratory housing.
evidence: This is a major conclusion of the study based on the enrichment effects observed.

claim: Salt-and-pepper organization is a robust feature of rodent L2/3 sensory maps, but its degree is flexible based on experience.
source: Enrichment reduced, but did not eliminate, salt-and-pepper tuning heterogeneity in L2/3. Thus, salt-and-pepper organization is a robust feature of rodent L2/3 sensory maps, but its degree is flexible based on experience.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the finding that enrichment reduced but did not abolish salt-and-pepper organization.

claim: Columns became more functionally independent after enrichment, which predicts more accurate column-based encoding of whisker input.
source: Enrichment reduced both mean tuning similarity and stimulus-independent (spontaneous) firing correlations across columns. Thus, columns became more functionally independent, which predicts more accurate column-based encoding of whisker input.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the correlation data and decoder analysis.

claim: GCaMP6s was expressed conditionally in layer-specific neurons using Cre lines.
source: We then characterized whisker tuning and somatotopic map organization in L2/3 or L4 excitatory cells using 2-photon imaging of GCaMP6s expressed conditionally using layer-specific Cre lines.
evidence: This describes the experimental approach used in the study.

claim: Enrichment greatly enhances columnar organization in L2/3 of S1.
source: Thus, enrichment greatly enhances columnar organization in L2/3 of S1, so that cellular-scale functional topography better matches the anatomical columnar map.
evidence: This is a major conclusion of the study based on the enrichment effects observed.

claim: After enrichment, cellular-scale functional topography better matches the anatomical columnar map in L2/3.
source: Thus, enrichment greatly enhances columnar organization in L2/3 of S1, so that cellular-scale functional topography better matches the anatomical columnar map.
evidence: This is a major conclusion of the study.

claim: Whisker-evoked ΔF/F responses were measured from regions of interest corresponding to GCaMP6-expressing somata.
source: Whisker-evoked ΔF/F responses were measured from regions of interest (ROI) corresponding to GCaMP6-expressing somata.
evidence: This describes the measurement method used in the study.

claim: ROIs were considered significantly whisker-responsive if the distribution of whisker-evoked ΔF/F was greater than blank trials (permutation test, α = 0.05 corrected for nine whiskers).
source: ROIs were considered significantly whisker-responsive if the distribution of whisker-evoked ΔF/F (quantified in a 1 s period after whisker deflection) was greater than blank trials (permutation test, α = 0.05 corrected for nine whiskers, see Materials and methods).
evidence: This describes the statistical criterion for identifying responsive neurons.

claim: Imaged neurons were localized post-hoc relative to column boundaries by histological staining and alignment by surface blood vessels.
source: Imaged neurons were localized post-hoc relative to column boundaries by histological staining and alignment by surface blood vessels (Figure 1E).
evidence: This describes the method for localizing neurons to anatomical columns.

claim: Enriched mice were housed with 2–3 littermates in standard mouse cages with nesting enclosure and several toys that were exchanged every 2–4 days.
source: EN animals were housed with 2–3 littermates in standard mouse cages (30 × 14 × 18 cm) into which a nesting enclosure and several toys were added and exchanged every 2–4 days.
evidence: This describes the enrichment housing protocol.

claim: Toys included sticks and blocks made from wood, ridged plastic, PVC, rubber, or cement, chosen for diversity of shape and texture.
source: Toys included sticks and blocks made from wood, ridged plastic, PVC, rubber, or cement, chosen for diversity of shape and texture (Figure 1A, Figure 1—figure supplement 1–).
evidence: This describes the types of enrichment toys used.

claim: Normally housed mice were housed with one littermate and no toys.
source: NH mice were housed in the same cage, with one littermate and no toys.
evidence: This describes the normal housing protocol.

claim: A single surgery for headgear implant and viral injection was performed at approximately P41 for Drd3-Cre mice or approximately P30 for Scnn1a-Cre mice.
source: A single surgery for headgear implant and viral injection was performed at ~P41 (Drd3-Cre mice) or ~P30 (Scnn1a-Cre mice).
evidence: This describes the surgical timeline.

claim: Intrinsic signal imaging was performed through the intact skull to localize D1, D2 and D3 columns in S1.
source: Intrinsic signal imaging (ISOI) was performed through the intact skull to localize D1, D2 and D3 columns in S1 (Drew and Feldman, 2009), and a 3 mm craniotomy was made over the D2 column.
evidence: This describes the method for localizing barrel columns before surgery.

claim: For L2/3 imaging in Drd3-Cre mice, AAV1-Syn-Flex-GCaMP6S-WPRE was injected at approximately 200 and 300 µm below the dura.
source: For L2/3 (Drd3-Cre mice), we used AAV1-Syn-Flex-GCaMP6S-WPRE, injected at ~200 and ~300 µm below the dura.
evidence: This describes the viral injection protocol for L2/3 labeling.

claim: For L4 imaging in Scnn1a-Cre mice, AAV9-CAG-Flex-GCaMP6s-WPRE was injected at approximately 350 and 450 µm below the dura.
source: For L4 (Scnn1a-Cre mice), we used AAV9-CAG-Flex-GCaMP6s-WPRE, injected ~350 and ~450 µm below the dura.
evidence: This describes the viral injection protocol for L4 labeling.

claim: Mice recovered to pre-surgical weight within 4 days (normally housed) or 5.5 days (enriched), on average.
source: Mice recovered to pre-surgical weight within 4 days (NH) or 5.5 days (EN), on average.
evidence: This is a quantitative result from surgical recovery monitoring.

claim: The prevalence of exploratory behaviors did not differ between enriched and normally housed mice during surgical recovery.
source: The prevalence of these behaviors did not differ between EN and NH mice, although EN mice showed a non-significant trend for more locomotor behavior (data not shown).
evidence: This is a result from behavioral monitoring during recovery.

claim: Imaging was performed under low-dose isoflurane (<1% in oxygen) combined with the sedative chlorprothixene (0.08 mg, i.p.).
source: Imaging was performed under low-dose isoflurane (<1% in oxygen) combined with the sedative chlorprothixene (0.08 mg, i.p.), with body temperature stabilized at 37°C.
evidence: This describes the anesthesia protocol for imaging.

claim: L2/3 imaging fields were approximately 400 × 400 μm, located approximately 100–250 µm below the dura, and contained approximately 50–100 expressing neurons.
source: L2/3 imaging fields were ~400 × 400 μm, located ~100–250 µm below the dura, and contained ~50–100 expressing neurons.
evidence: This describes the imaging field characteristics for L2/3.

claim: Whisker stimuli were presented as trains of five impulses, 100 ms apart, with individual deflections of 300 µm rostrocaudal deflection, rise/fall time 4 ms, total duration 10 ms.
source: Whisker stimuli were presented as trains (five impulses, 100 ms apart) of individual deflections (300 µm rostrocaudal deflection, rise/fall time 4 ms, total duration 10 ms).
evidence: This describes the whisker stimulus parameters.

claim: Trains are necessary due to sparse spiking in L2/3.
source: Trains are necessary due to sparse spiking in L2/3 (de Kock et al., 2007; Barth and Poulet, 2012), and increase the likelihood of eliciting detectable GCaMP signals.
evidence: This is justified by citations to prior work on L2/3 spiking properties.

claim: The nine whisker stimuli plus 'blank' trials were interleaved with 5 s inter-stimulus interval in random order.
source: We interleaved the nine whisker stimuli (5 s isi, random order) plus 'blank' trials in which no whisker was deflected.
evidence: This describes the stimulus presentation protocol.

claim: At each imaging field, 60 ± 10 repetitions of each whisker stimulus were presented.
source: At each imaging field, 60 ± 10 repetitions of each whisker stimulus were presented, and imaging data was collected as approximately forty 80 s long movies.
evidence: This describes the number of stimulus repetitions.

claim: Genetic expression of GCaMP is unlikely to affect basic L2/3 map development, because salt-and-pepper organization has also been observed with acute loading of OGB-1 AM.
source: Genetic expression of GCaMP is unlikely to affect basic L2/3 map development, because salt-and-pepper organization has also been observed with acute loading of OGB-1 AM, rather than genetic expression of GCaMP (Clancy et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to a prior study using a different calcium indicator.

claim: Only 4% of cells in Drd3-Cre mice and 1.2% of cells in Scnn1a-Cre mice showed nuclear GCaMP fluorescence indicative of GCaMP overexpression, and were excluded from analysis.
source: Only 4% of cells in Drd3-Cre mice and 1.2% of cells in Scnn1a-Cre mice showed nuclear GCaMP fluorescence indicative of GCaMP overexpression, and were excluded from analysis.
evidence: This describes quality control for GCaMP expression.

claim: For juxtacellular recordings, a non-Cre-dependent GCaMP6s virus (AAV1-Syn-Flex-GCaMP6S-WPRE) was injected at approximately 200 and 300 µm below the dura.
source: For simultaneous imaging and cell attached recordings, we injected a non-Cre-dependent GCaMP6s virus (AAV1-Syn-Flex-GCaMP6S-WPRE) at ~200 and ~300 µm below the dura at one stereotaxic location in S1.
evidence: This describes the viral injection protocol for calibration experiments. Note: there appears to be an error in the manuscript text - it says 'non-Cre-dependent' but lists a Flex (Cre-dependent) virus.

claim: Imaging movies were corrected for slow XY motion using dftregistration.
source: Imaging movies were corrected for slow XY motion in Matlab using dftregistration (Guizar-Sicairos et al., 2008) (Matlab file exchange).
evidence: This describes the motion correction method with a citation.

claim: Substantial Z-axis motion was not observed during imaging.
source: We did not observe substantial Z-axis motion.
evidence: This is an observation about imaging quality.

claim: For L4 ROIs, mean fluorescence of the neuropil mask was scaled by 0.3 and subtracted from the raw somatic ROI fluorescence.
source: For L4 ROIs, mean fluorescence of the neuropil mask was scaled by 0.3 and subtracted from the raw somatic ROI fluorescence.
evidence: This describes the neuropil subtraction method for L4.

claim: For L2/3 ROIs, neuropil subtraction was not used in the main analysis.
source: For L2/3 ROIs, neuropil subtraction was not used in the main analysis, but is presented in Figure 5—figure supplement 2.
evidence: This describes the neuropil subtraction approach for L2/3.

claim: A ROI was considered whisker responsive if it was significantly responsive to at least one whisker above baseline activity.
source: A ROI was considered whisker responsive if it was significantly responsive to at least one whisker above baseline activity.
evidence: This describes the criterion for including neurons in analysis.

claim: Signal correlation was defined as the Pearson's correlation of Z-scored response vectors for a pair of neurons.
source: To compute signal correlation, we calculated for each ROI a 9-element vector composed of its mean response to each whisker over all stimulus repetitions. Each vector was individually Z-scored. Signal correlation was defined as the Pearson's correlation of the vectors for a pair of neurons.
evidence: This describes the method for computing signal correlation.

claim: Noise correlation was computed as the mean Pearson's correlation across all whiskers for trial-to-trial response variability between neuron pairs.
source: To compute noise correlations, we constructed for each ROI, nine vectors (one for each whisker) containing the mean ΔF/F during the evoked window following each stimulus iteration. Each vector was individually z-scored. We computed the Pearson's correlation for each pair of neurons separately for each whisker, then computed the mean correlation for all whiskers.
evidence: This describes the method for computing noise correlation.

claim: Each ROI was represented by nine binary classifiers that were trained by logistic regression to report the probability of a stimulus given the mean ΔF/F during a single trial.
source: Each ROI was represented by a nine binary classifiers – one per whisker – that were trained by logistic regression to report the probability of a stimulus given the mean ΔF/F during the evoked window following a single whisker deflection, selected randomly from each stimulus iteration (structured as in McGuire et al., 2016).
evidence: This describes the neural decoder construction method.

claim: For ensemble decoding, the output of each ROI classifier was normalized so that each unit had the same weight in population decoding.
source: To predict single-trial stimuli from ensembles, the output of each ROI classifier was normalized so that each unit had the same weight in population decoding.
evidence: This describes the ensemble decoder method.

claim: Single-ROI decoders performed above chance, with slightly better performance by enriched cells than normally housed cells (fraction correct for NH: 0.63 ± 0.005, for EN: 0.65 ± 0.004, p=0.004).
source: Single-ROI decoders performed above chance, with slightly better performance by EN cells than NH cells (fraction correct for NH: 0.63 ± 0.005, for EN: 0.65 ± 0.004, p=0.004, permutation test for difference in means).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the decoder analysis.

claim: Detection performance increased with population size and was greater for enriched than normally housed mice for populations containing ≥3 neurons (p<0.001).
source: Detection performance increased with population size, and was greater for EN than NH for populations containing ≥3 neurons (p<0.001; permutation test of difference in means) (Figure 7A–C).
evidence: This is a quantitative result from the population decoder analysis shown in Figure 7C.

claim: Mean detection performance was greatest for ensembles centered near the whisker column center and fell off with distance.
source: Mean detection performance (on average across the population sizes) was greatest for ensembles centered near the whisker column center, and fell off with distance.
evidence: This is a result from the spatially-organized decoder analysis shown in Figure 7D.

claim: The strengthening and sharpening of the point representation in enriched mice improves single-trial population detection of whisker deflections inside each whisker's column.
source: Thus, the strengthening and sharpening of the point representation in EN mice improves single-trial population detection of whisker deflections inside each whisker's column, and topographically sharpens effective decoding in S1.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the decoder analysis in Figure 7.

claim: Enrichment topographically sharpens effective decoding in S1.
source: Thus, the strengthening and sharpening of the point representation in EN mice improves single-trial population detection of whisker deflections inside each whisker's column, and topographically sharpens effective decoding in S1.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the decoder analysis in Figure 7D.

claim: S1 of normally housed mice exhibits dispersed, salt-and-pepper tuning organization in L2/3, without functional borders at column boundaries.
source: Our findings confirm that S1 of NH mice exhibits dispersed, salt-and-pepper tuning organization in L2/3, without functional borders at column boundaries (Sato et al., 2007; Clancy et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a conclusion supported by the experimental data and citations to prior work.

claim: Whisker somatotopy is more precise in L4 but more dispersed in L2/3, similar to tonotopy in rodent A1.
source: Thus, whisker somatotopy is more precise in L4 but more dispersed in L2/3, similar to tonotopy in rodent A1 (Winkowski and Kanold, 2013).
evidence: This is a conclusion comparing whisker somatotopy to auditory tonotopy, with a citation.

claim: GCaMP6- and spike-based tuning measurements differ because of lower single-spike sensitivity with GCaMP and the use of train stimuli rather than single whisker deflections.
source: GCaMP6- and spike-based tuning measurements will differ because of lower single-spike sensitivity with GCaMP, and the use of train stimuli rather than single whisker deflections.
evidence: This is a discussion of methodological limitations.

claim: Some non-columnar whisker responses in GCaMP imaging may reflect slow tangential activity propagation across columns within the 1 s response window.
source: In addition, some non-columnar whisker responses in GCaMP imaging may reflect slow tangential activity propagation across columns (Petersen et al., 2003) within the 1 s response window.
evidence: This is a discussion of a potential confound, with a citation to prior work.

claim: Imaging is essential to measure map topography among pyramidal cells, because dense, cell-type specific recording with accurate soma localization is generally not possible using spike recordings.
source: Imaging is essential to measure map topography among PYR cells, because dense, cell-type specific recording with accurate soma localization is generally not possible using spike recordings.
evidence: This is a justification for the imaging approach based on technical limitations of electrophysiology.

claim: Enrichment can weaken and spatially sharpen whisker responses.
source: Enrichment can weaken and spatially sharpen whisker responses (Polley et al., 2004), or promote larger, more overlapping whisker responses (Guic et al., 2008), and can create smoother maps of cutaneous forepaw input (Coq and Xerri, 1998).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies on enrichment effects.

claim: Enrichment can promote larger, more overlapping whisker responses.
source: Enrichment can weaken and spatially sharpen whisker responses (Polley et al., 2004), or promote larger, more overlapping whisker responses (Guic et al., 2008), and can create smoother maps of cutaneous forepaw input (Coq and Xerri, 1998).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Guic et al., 2008.

claim: Enrichment can create smoother maps of cutaneous forepaw input.
source: Enrichment can weaken and spatially sharpen whisker responses (Polley et al., 2004), or promote larger, more overlapping whisker responses (Guic et al., 2008), and can create smoother maps of cutaneous forepaw input (Coq and Xerri, 1998).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Coq and Xerri, 1998.

claim: Map changes in L2/3 from enrichment could reflect use-dependent strengthening of L4-L2/3 or local recurrent projections.
source: In L2/3, map changes could reflect use-dependent strengthening of L4-L2/3 or local recurrent projections (Clem and Barth, 2006; Ko et al., 2013), reorganization of cross-columnar projections (Finnerty et al., 1999), or changes in POm thalamic (Audette et al., 2019) or top-down input (LeMessurier and Feldman, 2018) to L2/3.
evidence: This is speculation about potential mechanisms, supported by citations to relevant prior work.

claim: Map changes in L2/3 from enrichment could reflect reorganization of cross-columnar projections.
source: In L2/3, map changes could reflect use-dependent strengthening of L4-L2/3 or local recurrent projections (Clem and Barth, 2006; Ko et al., 2013), reorganization of cross-columnar projections (Finnerty et al., 1999), or changes in POm thalamic (Audette et al., 2019) or top-down input (LeMessurier and Feldman, 2018) to L2/3.
evidence: This is speculation about potential mechanisms, supported by a citation.

claim: Map changes in L2/3 from enrichment could reflect changes in POm thalamic input to L2/3.
source: In L2/3, map changes could reflect use-dependent strengthening of L4-L2/3 or local recurrent projections (Clem and Barth, 2006; Ko et al., 2013), reorganization of cross-columnar projections (Finnerty et al., 1999), or changes in POm thalamic (Audette et al., 2019) or top-down input (LeMessurier and Feldman, 2018) to L2/3.
evidence: This is speculation about potential mechanisms, supported by a citation.

claim: Map changes in L2/3 from enrichment could reflect changes in top-down input to L2/3.
source: In L2/3, map changes could reflect use-dependent strengthening of L4-L2/3 or local recurrent projections (Clem and Barth, 2006; Ko et al., 2013), reorganization of cross-columnar projections (Finnerty et al., 1999), or changes in POm thalamic (Audette et al., 2019) or top-down input (LeMessurier and Feldman, 2018) to L2/3.
evidence: This is speculation about potential mechanisms, supported by a citation.

claim: Several prior studies found that enrichment enhances whisker-evoked spiking and local field potential responses in whisker S1.
source: Several prior studies found that enrichment enhances whisker-evoked spiking and local field potential responses in whisker S1, but did not measure effects on receptive fields or maps (Alwis and Rajan, 2014; Devonshire et al., 2010; Megevand et al., 2009).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies.

claim: Enhanced magnitude of whisker responses from enrichment matches prior findings in auditory and visual cortex.
source: This enhanced magnitude of whisker responses echoes prior findings in auditory and visual cortex (Alwis and Rajan, 2014), matches our findings in L2/3 (Figures 2 and 4), and may involve spine formation induced by enrichment in S1 (Landers et al., 2011).
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior work and the current study's data.

claim: Enhanced whisker responses from enrichment may involve spine formation induced by enrichment in S1.
source: This enhanced magnitude of whisker responses echoes prior findings in auditory and visual cortex (Alwis and Rajan, 2014), matches our findings in L2/3 (Figures 2 and 4), and may involve spine formation induced by enrichment in S1 (Landers et al., 2011).
evidence: This is speculation about mechanisms, supported by a citation to prior work on spine formation.

claim: One study used intrinsic signal imaging to discover sharpened whisker point representations in L2/3 after adult enrichment, caused by reduction of whisker response magnitude and sharpening of L2/3 single-unit receptive fields.
source: One study used intrinsic signal imaging to discover sharpened whisker point representations in L2/3 after adult enrichment, caused by reduction of whisker response magnitude and sharpening of L2/3 single-unit receptive fields (Polley et al., 2004).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to Polley et al., 2004.

claim: Cellular-resolution mapping substantially extends prior findings by showing that juvenile enrichment strengthens columnar whisker responses, sharpens the L2/3 whisker map, and generates functional tuning boundaries in L2/3 aligned to anatomical column edges.
source: Our cellular-resolution mapping substantially extends this finding, by showing that juvenile enrichment strengthens CW responses, sharpens the L2/3 whisker map, and generates functional tuning boundaries in L2/3 aligned to anatomical column edges.
evidence: This is a statement of the study's contribution relative to prior work.

claim: Cellular-resolution imaging detected modest receptive field plasticity in L4, which was not detected in L4 multiunit recordings in a prior study.
source: By imaging in L4, we detected modest receptive field plasticity, which was not detected in L4 multiunit recordings (Polley et al., 2004).
evidence: This compares the current findings to prior work, with a citation.

claim: Differences between the current study and prior work could reflect enrichment age or species (mice vs. rats).
source: These differences could also reflect enrichment age or species (mice vs. rats).
evidence: This is speculation about potential reasons for differences from prior studies.

claim: Layer-specific population calcium imaging allowed observation of map sharpening among diversely tuned neurons.
source: Layer-specific population Ca imaging allowed us to observe map sharpening among diversely tuned neurons, and to discover that enrichment regulates the degree of salt-and-pepper organization in S1.
evidence: This is a statement about the advantages of the imaging approach used in the study.

claim: The current study discovered that enrichment regulates the degree of salt-and-pepper organization in S1.
source: Layer-specific population Ca imaging allowed us to observe map sharpening among diversely tuned neurons, and to discover that enrichment regulates the degree of salt-and-pepper organization in S1.
evidence: This is a statement of a key finding of the study.

claim: S1 contains whisker-specific thalamocortical termination zones in L4.
source: S1 contains whisker-specific thalamocortical termination zones in L4 (Woolsey and Van der Loos, 1970) and strong radial L4-L2/3 connectivity (Bender et al., 2003; Bureau et al., 2006).
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge supported by citations.

claim: S1 contains strong radial L4-L2/3 connectivity.
source: S1 contains whisker-specific thalamocortical termination zones in L4 (Woolsey and Van der Loos, 1970) and strong radial L4-L2/3 connectivity (Bender et al., 2003; Bureau et al., 2006).
evidence: This is established anatomical knowledge supported by citations.

claim: Greater differentiation of somatotopic tuning across columns could improve neural coding for whisker stimulus detection in each column.
source: Greater differentiation of somatotopic tuning across columns could improve neural coding for whisker stimulus detection in each column.
evidence: This is a prediction based on coding theory principles.

claim: Noise correlations are often detrimental for sensory coding.
source: In addition, because noise correlations are often detrimental for sensory coding (Kohn et al., 2016), their reduction may improve whisker sensory coding for downstream areas.
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work on noise correlations and coding.

claim: Reduction of noise correlations across columns may improve whisker sensory coding for downstream areas.
source: In addition, because noise correlations are often detrimental for sensory coding (Kohn et al., 2016), their reduction may improve whisker sensory coding for downstream areas.
evidence: This is a prediction based on the observed reduction in noise correlations and coding theory.

claim: Reduced signal and noise correlations across columns in L2/3 may reflect more rigid columnar segregation of L4-L2/3 and L2/3-L2/3 circuits.
source: Reduced signal and noise correlations across columns in L2/3 may reflect more rigid columnar segregation of L4-L2/3 and L2/3-L2/3 circuits, for example by reducing cross-columnar excitatory projections or enhancing cross-columnar inhibition.
evidence: This is speculation about potential circuit mechanisms underlying the observed changes.

claim: Increased signal correlations within L4 columns from enrichment may reflect stronger recurrent excitation in each L4 barrel.
source: In L4, enrichment increased signal correlations within columns, which may reflect stronger recurrent excitation in each L4 barrel (Ashby and Isaac, 2011).
evidence: This is speculation about mechanisms, supported by a citation to prior work on L4 recurrent connectivity.

claim: Single L2/3 neurons in S1 exhibit high trial-to-trial response variability.
source: Single L2/3 neurons in S1 exhibit high trial-to-trial response variability (de Kock et al., 2007; Barth and Poulet, 2012), which limits coding efficiency.
evidence: This is supported by citations to prior studies on L2/3 response variability.

claim: High trial-to-trial response variability in L2/3 neurons limits coding efficiency.
source: Single L2/3 neurons in S1 exhibit high trial-to-trial response variability (de Kock et al., 2007; Barth and Poulet, 2012), which limits coding efficiency.
evidence: This is an inference based on coding theory and the cited variability.

claim: L2/3 pyramidal cell ensembles relay information from S1 to downstream cortical areas.
source: Our focus was on coding by L2/3 PYR cell ensembles, which relay information from S1 to downstream cortical areas (Chen et al., 2015).
evidence: This is supported by a citation to prior work on L2/3 output projections.

claim: The decoder results do not predict whether behavioral detection of whisker input is altered by enrichment.
source: These results do not predict whether behavioral detection of whisker input is altered by enrichment, but they do suggest that coding within individual S1 columns is more efficient.
evidence: This is a caveat about the interpretation of the decoder results.

claim: The decoder results suggest that coding within individual S1 columns is more efficient after enrichment.
source: These results do not predict whether behavioral detection of whisker input is altered by enrichment, but they do suggest that coding within individual S1 columns is more efficient.
evidence: This is a conclusion based on the decoder analysis in Figure 7.

claim: The enriched environment likely increases social interactions and affects general activity levels in addition to promoting more diverse tactile experience.
source: While enrichment promotes more diverse tactile experience, it also likely increases social interactions and affects general activity levels.
evidence: This is an inference about the multiple factors affected by enrichment.

claim: Which factors (tactile experience, social interactions, or activity levels) are dominant in driving whisker map plasticity was not tested.
source: Which of these factors is dominant in driving whisker map plasticity was not tested.
evidence: This is a statement about a limitation of the study.

claim: The circuit mechanisms for emergence of columnar structure in L2/3 remain to be identified.
source: The circuit mechanisms for emergence of columnar structure in L2/3 remain to be identified.
evidence: This is a statement about future research directions.
